rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken equivalent of “strange” or “odd.”

example.english: The decor in this shop is peculiar—I don’t know what to say.
example.traditional: 呢間舖啲擺設好奇怪，睇到我唔知講咩好。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 di1 baai2 cit3 hou2 kei4 gwaai3 tai2 dou3 ngo5 m4 zi1 gong2 me1 hou2

rows.note: Use this when something seems distinctly odd, weird, or unconventional rather than merely unexpected.

example.english: Their laugh is really peculiar; it gives me goosebumps.
example.traditional: 佢個笑聲真係好古怪，聽到我起雞皮。
example.jyutping: keoi5 go3 siu3 sing1 zan1 hai6 hou2 gu2 gwaai3 teng1 dou3 ngo5 hei2 gai1 pei4

rows.note: Use this for something characteristic of or exclusive to a particular place or circumstance, not for something strange.

example.english: This aroma is peculiar to this place.
example.traditional: 呢種香味係呢個地方特有嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 zung2 hoeng1 mei6 hai6 ni1 go3 dei6 fong1 dak6 jau5 ge3
